messages.author: 865451ff948b0e2a
messages.subject: problem loading forecast library
parts:
I have this in my R.conf
REvalOnStartup "library(phpSerialize); library(forecast)"

On apache restart I get this in apache error.log

Loading required package: tseries
Error: package 'tseries' could not be loaded
In addition: Warning message:
In library(pkg, character.only = TRUE, logical.return = TRUE, lib.loc = lib.loc) :
  there is no package called 'tseries'
 From directive REvalOnStartup on line 11 of /etc/apache2/mods-enabled/r.conf.
Loading required package: tseries

tseries is a library required by Forecast. I've tried to reinstall and the library loads from R itself.

Any suggestions? thanks

messages.author: 25a4f5811cd7d59e
messages.subject: Re: problem loading forecast library
parts:
Make sure that you are installing packages into system-wide areas like
/usr/lib/R/library, /usr/lib/R/site-library, and/or
/usr/local/lib/R/site-library.

I know that when you run R as yourself (not root) it can place your
personal package area first in the library path list. For instance on
my computer, when I run .libPaths(), I get this:

> .libPaths()
[1] "/home/hornerj/R/i486-pc-linux-gnu-library/2.12"
[2] "/usr/local/lib/R/site-library"
[3] "/usr/lib/R/site-library"
[4] "/usr/lib/R/library"

So if I were to install forecast, it would go in the first path listed
above and my rApache install would not be able to use it.

Best,

Jeff

messages.author: 42eed4e1caba0ad0
messages.subject: Re: problem loading forecast library
parts:
You can apply this quick "hack" in order to see the installation path of a package:

pkg <- installed.packages()
pkg[which(pkg[, 1] == "brew"), 2]  ## I used brew, so change it to "forecast"

See manual pages for installed.packages

Best,
Alex

messages.author: 42eed4e1caba0ad0
messages.subject: Re: problem loading forecast library
parts:
You can add yourself in group "staff":

# adduser <yourusername> staff

afterwards, you can install packages it /usr/lib/  folders, since "staff" has write permissions there.
